disease_label_per_paper: Group A streptococcal toxic shock syndrome after routine gynecological procedure
presentation_summary: 51-year-old postmenopausal woman developed fever, diarrhea and vomiting the day after gynecological examination with vaginal discharge and cytocervical sampling.
Seven days later she was transported to hospital with blood pressure 69/49 mmHg, respiratory rate 25/min, heart rate 62/min, temperature 37.7 C, oxygen saturation 93%, and GCS 15.
Physical exam revealed marked lower abdominal tenderness with guarding and no erythematous macular rash.
Labs on admission: WBC 12,100/uL, CRP 31.04 mg/dL, platelets 14.2 x10^4/uL, albumin 1.28 g/dL, BUN 83.6 mg/dL, creatinine 3.1 mg/dL, AST 96 U/L, ALT 30 U/L, LDH 801 U/L, CK 1027 U/L.

Ultrasound and CT showed intestinal edema, intestinal dilatation and large ascites; exploratory laparotomy found >2000 mL milky white purulent ascites without bowel necrosis or another abdominal source.

risk_context.source_text_value: gynecological examination with vaginal discharge and cytocervical sampling the day before symptom onset

observations.source_text_value: marked lower abdominal tenderness with muscle guarding
no erythematous macular rash was observed
recent gynecological examination with cytocervical sampling
noradrenaline and dopamine administered for severe septic shock
complete drainage and washing of the abdominal cavity
DIC diagnosed because of coagulopathy with platelet fall, FDP elevation and PT-INR prolongation
acute kidney injury on postoperative day 1 requiring continuous hemodiafiltration

confirmatory_findings.finding: Group A Streptococcus confirmed from sterile sites and vaginal swab
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: GAS was confirmed in blood, ascitic fluid, and vaginal swab specimens
patient was diagnosed with GAS-induced primary peritonitis and STSS caused by ascending vaginal infection

actual_treatment: exploratory laparotomy with drainage and abdominal washout
ampicillin plus clindamycin after GAS suspected/confirmed
thrombomodulin alfa and fresh frozen plasma for DIC
quality_warnings: This is a rash-negative STSS case; the absence of rash is retained rather than deleted.
GAS culture results are confirmatory_findings; ordinary evidence uses shock, GI symptoms, abdominal source, organ dysfunction and labs.
